newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs Monday seen steady-down -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs Monday seen steady-down -dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to lower, pressured by carryover weakness from this week's larger-than-expected marketings, livestock dealers said.
The large marketings weighed on pork prices and eroded packer operating margins, livestock dealers said.

Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa and southern Minnesota were seen ranging from $53.50 to $54.50 and top prices in Illinois for hogs to the plant could range from $53.00 to $53.50, sources in those areas said. Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at plants could range from $53.50 to $54.00.
Top plant prices for barrows and gilts in the interior Iowa/southern Minnesota area were $4.50-$5.00 lower for the week ended Friday, USDA said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota receipts this week totaled 577,000 head, up from 537,000 last week but below 589,000 last year, USDA said. The average hog weight for the week ended Oct 12 in the area was 250.6 lbs compared with 249.5 lbs the previous week and 249.0 last year.
Despite active hog marketings this week, increased weights indicated some producers were still busy in the fields and were delaying selling their hogs at optimal times.
Also, generally mild weather through the U.S. Midwest recently aided weight gains, sources noted.
USDA estimated the average weight of hogs slaughtered under federal inspection this week at 253 lbs, up three lbs from 250 lbs last week but still below the year-ago average of 256.
